q: Why did CAC increase yesterday? Check whether the change came from CPM, CTR, CPC, landing-page conversion, checkout conversion, product mix, or channel mix. Rank the drivers by likely contribution.
answer:
Short answer — the premise is incorrect: CAC fell, not rose. Measured CAC fell from ₹4,296 (2026-10-12) to ₹2,100 (2026-10-13), a −51.1% change. The drop was driven mostly by many more new customers; higher ad spend offset some of that improvement.

Key evidence (previous → yesterday)
- Ad spend: ₹38,661 → ₹50,404 (+30.4%) — Measured (paid_media)
- Impressions: 133,023 → 147,204 (+10.7%) — Measured (paid_media)
- Clicks: 3,433 → 4,234 (+23.4%) — Measured (paid_media)
- CTR: 2.6% → 2.9% (+11.4%) — Derived (measured clicks/impr)
- CPM: ₹291 → ₹343 (+17.8%) — Derived (measured) 
- CPC: ₹11 → ₹12 (+5.8%) — Derived (measured)
- Landing-page views (Meta only): 734 → 1,242 (+69.2%) — Measured (paid_media/meta)
- Landing-page view rate (LPVs ÷ clicks, Meta): 65.5% → 72.9% — Derived (measured)
- Checkout rate (site): 1.0% → 1.6% (+65.8%) — Measured (web_sessions)
- New customers: 9 → 24 (+166.7%) — Measured (commerce)
- CAC (ad spend ÷ new customers): ₹4,296 → ₹2,100 (−51.1%) — Derived (from measured ad spend & new customers)

Numeric decomposition (exact algebraic split of CAC change)
- Change in CAC = +₹1,305 due to higher ad spend (this pushed CAC up) — Derived
- Change in CAC = −₹3,500 due to more new customers (this pushed CAC down) — Derived
Net = −₹2,195 (matches measured CAC fall).

Ranked drivers (by likely contribution to the net CAC change)
1) New-customer increase (largest contributor to CAC falling) — Measured (new customers ↑ 166.7%). Likely caused by better funnel conversions below.  
2) Checkout conversion improvement — Measured (checkout rate +65.8%); likely the primary upstream cause of more new customers.  
3) Landing-page conversion / LPV rate (Meta) — Measured (LPV rate +11.4% on Meta); helped turn clicks into sessions/orders.  
4) Channel mix (more effective Meta spend and volume) — Measured: Meta new customers 4→14, Google 3→6; shifting spend to Meta amplified new-customer gains.  
5) CTR improvement — Measured (helped increase clicks → conversions).  
6) CPM / CPC increase — Measured (CPM +17.8%, CPC +5.8%); these raised cost per impression/click and partially offset CAC gains (explains the +₹1,305 opposing effect).  
7) Product mix — Partial evidence / Hypothesis: top products had product-level CACs ≈₹866–₹1,150 yesterday (product ad spend (allocated) ÷ product new customers); mix may have helped slightly but is not the dominant driver in the numbers above.

If you want, next I can:
- Run a diagnose_metric_change on new customers to rank upstream causes formally and return supported_cause / likely_contributor labels, or
- Produce a channel-by-channel CAC decomposition (hold mix constant vs actual) so we can quantify how much channel-mix vs within-channel performance moved CAC.
